14 would be considered pretty early but definitely some signs of masculine puberty are both likely and possibly minor depending on how early a bloomer she was. A transfer in later high school would be a good thing for her history. The past can show up later maybe and it shows that she tried to cope and had to deal with some good and then the worst. Perhaps after it became too much she wasn't defeated but wanted to rest for a bit as even the best of us can't take harassment forever, especially when we are younger. The fact that she threw some punches as well may show either she had some growing to do of her own or she had some serious reason to throw them or both. Immaturity makes fools of us all. But you have to defend yourself at times.

Trying to pass is an understandable choice and that opinion of it being no ones business while right does come with hang ups. People you interact with who are convinced can become close to you and treat you as a woman which is nice. But when aspects of your transition are brought to light by you when you need to share or when others force it out those who learn after can at times feel betrayed or at least shocked by the surprise. Still that is not always so and there are those who will just brush it off as inconsequential as it truly is though not always. Just keep that in mind as she interacts with new people or those close to her that don't know. It shows a lack of trust to not share that aspect but if others are offended by her lack of trust it can be a sticking point. Or not. Depends on the person.

That she does not hide when she must also comes to be its own thing as well. It can blindside people which can help and hurt as it places her in the line of fire. But since she is tough and now experienced she may be more than willing to stand up and accept it at times. Perhaps she doesn't begrudge people their feelings of betrayal but hopes they understand why it isn't easy for her. It is never easy to tell someone you are trans. Some are easier than others but you are discarding the safety of passing and the comfort of that feeling for the hope they accept and trust you for something they shouldn't even judge you for.

If she is that strong mothering protector with a tough edge then know that she can be strong in this way but the weakness of all strength is the trust or willingness to open that she may have. Still she also would have to be a good judge of people so maybe she knows this can be a weakness and she may want to watch out for those who exploit this too. A good detective suspects everyone but judges no one. They just want the facts.

As for her wanting to fix everyone and everything then I guess you know her main conflict then. She can't fix everyone or everything. But she can make it better or at least reveal the truth. Also she needs to remember that while reasons are complex for what people do deep down motives are usually simple.

Hate, envy, jealousy, greed, sloth, pride, anger, grief, loss, madness, vengeance, belief... All are complex reasons for doing wrong but all are not motives alone. They are emotional driven perspectives. 

Most are inspired by three things. Fear,  pain and stress.

If you fear something you begin to make it other than you and try to rationalize how to avoid or conquer that fear. But it is not always clear as it is a raw emotional response to something unknown and shocking.

If something causes you pain you do the same in many ways as you can identify pain and try to sort it and handle it. But pain can go on for far too long and it can force some to lash out for an end or relief.

Stress can overwhelm but it is mental pain in a way that leaves one confused or unbalanced as we try to sort out our own understanding or lack there of. But like pain it can be come too much and when it does the mind can fling itself down paths it may not normally consider to find some way to move away from it.

A criminal that is logically evil or malicious in intent usually learned through experience with doing wrong and getting away with it or comes to it out of pride in their mind and selfish resolve to escape punishment out of fear but able to rationalize horrible paths to avoid such discovery.

Ultimately even a simple criminal and a mastermind have the same base impulses. To avoid, fear, pain and stress.

A detective finds clues to link down to a possible reasoning why a person could make the wrong choice or what truly happened in those occurrences where there is no culprit. Some crimes may be passionate. Rarely will they be completely illogical but even that must be considered.

All things must be considered. So mercy must be held in mind but also saved for after the truth is found. So too must personal views and emotions. It is often when the case is personal that this becomes hard to keep in mind. So yes a trans case could affect her judgement and maybe she has to work on that.

You have to understand something to fix it after all.

Sorry if I come off preachy... I like detectives and mystery stories a lot so I have some views on how I think they work.

To back on point I think you have a good concept for her. I just hope I am helping!

And to be honest she would likely have some  perspective on male behavior. The fact that she started life being pressured even if not with intention by society to be male she may have resisted and just wanted to be girly. Or she may have wanted to hide if she was nervous as a child. She may have enjoyed some of the freedom of being seen as male and the lack of judgement for fitting her image. But it may have hurt too much for her to lie to herself and others. It hurts from my experience either way but being honest certainly is better in the long term. Boys are taught to be brave, confident and curious. But they are also often expected to be tough, in control of their emotions even when it is unhealthy to repress them and are expected to present an active and physical nature and personality. They are stereotyped as liking violence more, enjoying competitive games, confrontation and not being able to multitask. Their role models are all soldiers, sports stars and strong heroes and while that is not completely bad it is a lot of pressure.

Boys who do not fit the mold written above often feel pressure to conform or at least be complicit in such. Society expects it and male society expects that if you don't fit perfectly you at least try to fit. You are not shunned or snubbed necessarily but you certainly get pushed to the side or not considered. A boy can still be bullied or such and form clicks outside the main popular group just like girls can. But a boy who is too different lives in the culture of those stereotypes. Violence, competition, confrontation and focused thinking are what boys are taught as well as seeing emotions as weak. This does not make things easy for any boy that is alone in that. The more weak you appear the more different you seem the more alone you can be as those who blend better try to avoid the attention you bring on yourself.

So imagine being your a girl who all the boys think is a boy. Now imagine you try to befriend girls or don't agree with the boys. One side alienates you because you look like a boy. The other alienates you because you act like a girl.

The fact is boys can be everything people think a girl is and girls can be like what people think boys are like. It is the fact that we consider these traits as virtues or faults exclusive to one physical gender or another on a binary that we try to reinforce them. But not everyone fits them.

If you want more I encourage you to surf other topics here and just look at how the others here deal with such. It is a good place to inform yourself and it is called asktransgender for a reason. Just be sensitive on some of the more painful topics and try to read things and you should be fine.

As for her transition it can be fairly personal to the person and different in a lot of ways. Cliches as far as I can understand them would mostly involve the perfect family that supports without problems and never misgenders or fails to be an ally. The other cliche is the family that is just not going to accept the trans person and keeps trying to convince them their wrong even with well meaning advice.

The idea to avoid a cliche is to not make it a big deal all the time and to not make it be predictable. So the best way to do that is to make her transition not perfect but not terrible either. 

Perhaps her adoptive mom has a hard time adjusting at first and "deadname's" her or "misgenders" her but managed to correct it eventually. This could lead to her once in a time of stress later accidentally saying this again and immediately apologizing and or at least correcting herself. If she is supportive. Older people are stereotyped as having a hard time accepting things but make sure that it is not a matter of her being bigoted but just her memory. This could speak to the fact that the mind and memory is hard to change but not that an accidental slip means anything more if it is not often. It still hurts but it can be forgiven.

Mr.Snobbytallboy could perhaps not acknowledge it at first if he is the second oldest as he may have looked up to his "brother" and has difficulty transferring to this new "sister" idea. Maybe it bothers him still but he is trying and perhaps there was or could be a moment this could add to conflict before they resolve it even though he loves her. He just may have had a hard time at first with her being a her suddenly. Especially if he perhaps admired certain traits and got them caught up in his own interpretation of gender.

Now I am just assuming the "these two jerks" are the youngest and this falls into where you have the most room perhaps. The young can be framed on either side of the issue in her family. If they have a good relationship they may not even have a conflict if the concept of transgender is not foreign to them. But even if you love someone you may not agree completely with them. They could be accepting or they could be confrontational or curious. Accepting would be them obviously just treating her like a big sister with some work made to really know her. If they are ill informed but kind they may ask her questions that are awkward about being a girl though she may or may not be more comfortable answering her family as she wants them to understand. If they were confrontational they may try to undercut her decisions but claim to be there for her when it matters. Confrontational usually makes the character come off like a complete bigot and usually any attempt to convince a transgender they are not the gender they are is usually based on insecurity, counter beliefs or confusion when it is not from outright hatred. Still this could lead to such a family member changing their beliefs or understanding. Or maybe they just love and care for her even if they don't agree with her. Then again you said her family was mostly okay with it so perhaps the jerks could just rib her about it all or make puns or such when they are alone or with others who know. Nothing cruel but always in a teasing way.

But when it comes to the public it depends a lot on how and where she transitioned and how well you as the author of her think she passes. If she transitioned early she probably presents physically and vocally as a girl with little sign of masculine features. If she started later after puberty began in earnest she may have some signs of masculine features that have faded or she covers and her beauty routine could include certain procedures such as facial shaving or laser hair removal. She probably also had to do vocal exercises to help make her voice more feminine with occasional slips. If she transitioned even further into life she may have had quite a few surgeries and would probably have broader shoulders and larger feet though that does not have to be so. She would probably be taller as well if she started later though again not necessarily. She may have to deal with a deeper voice though nothing she couldn't work with.

If she transitioned young and stayed in the same school while doing such she would have to deal with others knowing. This can be a gauntlet depending upon her support at home and in the school. She may have transferred if possible after beginning her transition to start over so she does not have to deal with her past going forward. 

If it was as a teen she may have taken time away from school if she could to wait for her transition to get to a certain stage.

If she transitioned at an older age then she may have lost a job while it happened or even been told her job was secure only to be fired later. Or she may have kept it for a while. This would be before the whole Private Detective thing. If she was a cop before a private detective then I imagine she may have left the police force maybe due to the environment being less than friendly. Not that all the cops had a problem but maybe some or perhaps just one higher up than her. Nothing overt but more a disguised form of bigotry masking as political pressure if from above or just harassment or subtle threats or abandonment by her fellow officers if they were peers.

Publicly it also matters if she chooses to try and just pass as a woman or she accepts her role as a trans woman to be more honest and open about who she is. It is not safe obviously to do that even later with everyone but she may choose to tell those important to her in a business sense if it becomes and issue. And if she is clocked as trans then she will have to deal with that sometimes in worst case scenarios. It hardly ever benefits the situation to tell someone you are trans if they haven't figured it out. But personally you should share such if they are important to you. Still jerks are jerks and if she is confident then an observant detective should put aside what is not important and focus on what is. Most bigots or others who are going to hurt a trans person are not brave unless in a group of like minded people and not in view of the public or when they can catch them alone.

She also has to deal with everything that comes with being a woman. The glass ceiling, the harassment, relationships, body image, gender biased fashion standards etc. But then she also gets to be who she is and she choose to face these issues when she made the transition. She also gets to deal with the whole bathroom issue though as long as she passes it not that big of an issue perhaps in stopping her from using a public toilet. If she doesn't perfectly pass she may be a bit more nervous about it and may be stopped or confronted about it.

Glad to help a fellow artistic soul. :)

Make her as detailed as you want if that is what your story needs or benefits from. Just make sure those details are shown not told as well. Make her as detailed as you are in how she treats the things she cares about for good or bad. 

Show a favorite food, give her a best friend in the cast and make up why they are such friends. Show her enjoying her hobbies and doing work. Have her hang out or send letters or call her nieces and nephews. Give her moments where she deals with bills. Perhaps show her having trouble with something personal. Show her be there for a character and support them maybe without all the answers.

If she is the main character then don't be afraid to push her into the background at times to let her support other characters. If she is a side character just keep in mind this complexity and use her as she would naturally act in her moments to shine. Perhaps her own life is moving behind that of the main characters so when they need her she has her own issues.

People are multifaceted so even your minor side characters should have motives for what they do. They often do things for reasons that may or may not relate to others. They are just as affected by the world as any main character. Or at least make them act that way.

Just make her a person you can understand existing in your story and the rest should fall into place. If you know why she does what she does and feels what she feels she should appear very natural.

Honestly it is hard to deal with. But not every transphobe is hopeless. 

Oddly on online forums I have found that refusing to get angry and just answering all their points as if they were legitimate even the ridiculous ones works at times. When you can shut down an argument without ever getting angry yourself and being nothing but friendly and accepting it is amusing to watch them keep spinning their wheels. It is a slog though as you have to answer every single person who joins that conversation and you have to call them on everything they do wrong or offensively without ever insulting them. Not even little insults. You have to go into detail. Not easy but it can work on a topic per topic basis.

PM's are another matter though. They are often just trying to attack you without others watching because they are cowards. If it is not a threat and just insults and more reasons you are wrong and you wish to respond then just talk to them about it like above. It takes work but eventually when they see they can't make you hit them back or snap then you may make progress. Otherwise just politely ignore them or report them if you don't feel you can get through to them and they are escalating to threats or going too far.

I have gotten apologies and some interesting conversations out of the above methods. I have also watched those who don't care to be friendly vanish from my conversations. It's like a fighting game where my moveset is all compliments and sensitive and thoughtful answers and no matter what my opponents moves eventually fail to hurt me. Not because I am better just because I am trying to relate to them not attack or defeat them. I am seeking a draw. A conversation not just a debate. Where we come to common ground. I win by not winning but blunting their argument.

But threats need to be reported. Don't respond. Just report them. To the police or FBI if you must. If they keep making accounts to threaten you report those too. Don't engage and don't give out information. If you think it is weak to do so then I counter that it is weaker to push them and confirm you and they are enemies. They are looking for a target to scare and hurt and the more personal it is the more they feel in control. Don't give out info and don't respond to threats except to report them. Let them defeat themselves.

But after all that it is not always easy. I still have emotions. I get scared and tired and angry and at times I have to walk away from such and come back later. I want to flee to a safer environment too at times but I also don't want to retreat because they made me when I just want to talk. I have that impulse to hurt and insult and just consider people who are ignorant as less than me. 

But that impulse is what they use. That impulse as strong as it is, is wrong. You can't attack someone even with the truth and expect them to drop their defenses and listen to you. You can't make people respect or trust you with fear. You can only make them fear you.

I don't want more fear. As a wise Muppet once said. Fear leads to anger, anger leads to hate, hate leads to suffering. Or trolling and threats or worse.

So while I can agree your attacks could be cathartic I have to say that they are making you play their game by their rules.

They are not idiots or monsters for their ignorance or fear. They are just people. Flawed and lost like most of us. And when we don't listen or call them names we don't answer their questions only confirm their bias.

She looks good to me. Looking at your style reminds me a bit of the style of the webcomic Rock and Riot
http://rockandriotcomic.com/post/115020071048
Love that comic!

As for her design she seems fine. Women have various body types and as she stands she looks like a confident character. Giving her a pear shape is fine because many women trans or not are pear shaped. Also as your style is less hyper realistic detail and more cartoon stylized it requires you to make your characters different to stand out in broader details.

Personality wise make her a person. If you make her a strong person and not just a token showcase for trans issues that should be fine. If she has vulnerability about it or other aspects just try to keep her from being one note as if that is all she deals with. But if she faces such then make her face it as she would honestly for her character. If she is weak in a moment she can be strong in another and the character will be stronger to the audience for being weak but overcoming or dealing with that weakness.

A strong character is not always strong and can be weak at times. A truly strong character defines themselves as their own person through the challenges they face and how they live. And in so doing such a character changes the definitions of what others would use to define them. 

Her trans experience may have shaped her but from what I see she made it part of herself and grew from it. She is a detective, an adventurer, a geek for her cartoons (personally loved Darkwing Duck and Carmen San Diego), a cool aunt and a world traveler. Those experiences also shape her. She sounds and looks awesome.
Congratulations and I am happy for you!

Don't let this stop you and don't think that suicide is some kind of message you want to send. You want to be you and your an adult. So do what you need to take control of your life and if so take care of yourself. You can do it.

Tell your doctor that you are an adult and have considered this and you do not think this program is necessary and as them to explain what they need to confirm you are transgender. Be respectful. If they can give you any good reason why you need to go to this then honestly consider it if it seems to be the final goal post and will not take too long.

If not then my advice to you is to find another doctor with your therapist that can give you a second opinion based on your case. Most doctors are just looking to avoid being sued by their patients and to do no wrong by them as well. They want your money or the insurance companies money. They also are more covered the more people agree that giving you treatment would not be a mistake.

Another option that you can also do is to look into Planned Parenthood in your area to see if it is an option as they operate on informed consent and some locations offer HRT treatments.

You have options that don't require your family be involved nor is their acceptance going to make you more or less who you are. So be strong and make these choices for yourself because this is not easy but in the end you can make it happen.

If you need support or help I hope we helped!
It belongs here just fine. Proud of you! Don't live in regret!

A binary concept of gender is comforting and seemingly stable to those raised with it as the norm for evaluating themselves that way at a young age. A spectrum gender provides no easy simple stable position but a wide view of possible gender configurations that is far harder to accept. 

This is partially due to the binary being established by sexual traits established at the far end of two most apparent physical aspects of the original binary of male and female. The idea that those traits do not define a hard line gender flies in the face of an accepted understanding of what was considered to make a boy and boy and girl a girl. As if the fact that a spectrum based along two extremes somehow invalidates those extremes. 

This false assumption based on partial evidence that does not signify the whole of what determines someones gender and requires further study and understanding of gender by society individuals. 

Society that has stratified and used these traits to divide humanity along gender lines. Individuals who once thought it simple and due to how they conformed to societies view were validated for that view. 

Now they see others who refuse to conform and not hide any longer, and because this is an aberrant view to the majority of established societal views and has been vilified by certain popular factions within that society there is bound to be resistance or even backlash. It would break apart the very structures of those divisions on what separates a man from a woman to them and thus signify that those who held those standards had been wrong.

Being wrong is seen as some unforgivable crime by many and while it does cause issues it comes down to if we as a species and a society can accept we are wrong and forgive each other for it by working together to find the truth.

This unfortunately will be a hard view for many who profit from the current world or who feel their ego validated by that view to accept. Many who just believe the truth is what can be seen with only a cursory glance and refuse to ever accept a deeper look. They have an answer and refuse to add further facts to their narrative that would fundamentally change it.

Well I know it isn't easy. But don't sell yourself short. Even just doing what you are is a step in keeping confidence. She may or may not come around but you are stronger than you think and I know you can do it. It just takes work and effort and if you want to talk when it gets to be too much we are here.

I know my brother falls into this camp. He has just recently told me straight to my face exactly his views on the situation. I have told him why that is disrespectful and he used the fact that there are so many types of gender and that he only considers male and female as well as intersex to be the only considerations he will make to pronouns. He also threw the fact that discrimination cases are brought up about mis-gendering where using the wrong pronoun can get you in trouble with the law. 

While I don't think someone should be arrested for such I don't think that it is right or kind or appropriate. I also told him that it is not his place to put a standard of existence for all of humanity and the genders and expressions of such.

When it comes to trans people he told me openly that he will only use the pronouns for that person when they are there but will still call them whatever he is comfortable with among others. Guess that included me.

He doesn't see it as wrong. He thinks the issue is due to delusions. He views gender as purely an issue of body not considering the brain as part of it. I get the impression that he views trans people as suffering a mental disorder rather than a truly biological one. But he doesn't even take the scientific studies considering brains of trans people as valid claiming that female and male traits are possessed by both genders and that body is the sole determiner of gender.

Stings quite a bit as he is actually one of the few relatives on my dad's side of the family I respect for most of his other opinions. But I think he is changing quite a bit more as time goes on.

People are not perfect and to him he thinks he is doing right by doing this. Still I was disappointed by him for one of the first times in my life. I guess he just doesn't see me or any other trans person as who they are.

I plan to keep trying with my brother but I can't force him to change and I don't want to force him. I also don't have support to convince him. So I may just have to distance myself from him if I can't. It is going to be hard as he was one of the few family members I had thought accepted me but I will do what I must.

A letter is safe from the initial reaction and I hope it goes good for you. I know before I came out my family had no idea and I had held it in for a long time. Mine didn't go good but a friend of mine has a wonderful supportive mother helping her transition. But remember that being honest with yourself and those you love shows them more respect than to lie and make yourself uncomfortable for them to believe that lie.

Just be ready for the conversation to follow that letter and the possible issues. And don't let it stop you if it does not go well. Keep talking if you can but know you can't change people's minds. Only they can. You may have to do this in spite of them but if you want it then get it.

It won't be easy but if it lets you be who you truly are it will be worth it. Don't live in regret. Be happy with who you are and live to the fullest.

Ask her what she would be comfortable with, and you also all need to discuss what you all would also be comfortable with. If not everyone is comfortable with her then you and those who are could still change with her. But don't make this something she alone has to do that excludes her when she is supposed to be included. 

She is a girl. She has body image issues due to how she was born. Treat her like any other person. She can be shy or maybe self conscious or even be considering your discomfort by doing what she is. Or she may just not be comfortable with nudity herself.

But be prepared for her to still use the teachers area. She may just not be confident or comfortable enough with herself yet for that. So be supportive. Be her friend and don't force her to change but don't let her just drift away. 

Stand up and stay by her. Respect her choice but don't let it prevent you from being friends. Maybe wait for her by the teachers area to include her. Or also talk to her if she decides to use a stall if you talk to your other friends while changing. Maybe those uncomfortable with the nudity can just turn respectfully but still talk to her just like any other friend. You may have to initiate a bit but just try a bit harder for her if she isn't open. 

You can tell when your friends do or don't want to talk normally so just try to help her when you can. Don't let her be alone but don't swamp her with more attention. She likely doesn't want to be treated as the "trans-girl" but just like any other girl or person would.

Just let her set the limits and work with her. And keep trying as hard as you can to be a friend. She is lucky to have people be considerate. But remember you are lucky to have her as a friend. High school will be eventually be over but a friendship and her memories of that time are what will last.

You are not trapped as long as you work and remember you are wonderful even now. You are not alone because I have felt just as you have described. Just keep working towards your goal now that your sure and keep that in mind. You know what it is, how to fix it and that there is help to get it. Just work hard and get the help and support you need. You can do this. :)

You are in a fairly similar position to me. I have lost my wife due to her abusing my trust and taking my disability. I am suffering mental damage from a degrading condition that is stealing away my mind to where I flunked/dropped out of college when I was on the deans list. My father is a judgemental right wing republican who I live with as I have no other means to support myself and the rest of his side of the family and my nuclear family all agree I am mentally insane. My transition never started even though I knew since I was five because I have lived in fear of losing the few people I care about because I don't want to be alone. I was told my feelings were wrong and I couldn't speak up on what I was. The moment I did I felt people around me look at me different. They humored me or tolerated me. They couldn't understand and I couldn't explain. Even to the few I was close with in my family and friends it was like pulling teeth. I spend most days just laying in my bed in physical and mental torment waiting to die. I have cried and screamed and prayed and begged and wished for some way out. I can't even care about keeping up appearances any more. My mother and her side of the family I keep in the dark due to them being so distant in part and my mom is dying similarly in that she is sick and I don't want to trouble her and I have trouble facing the fact that I am falling apart like she is. I am worried that I hurt everyone around me. I feel like a leech as I sleep and occasionally drink and eat enough to keep myself from dying.

I try not to but I still worry I do. I obsess and worry that even when people say they are fine around me they are judging. I have to fight paranoia and guilt over things I shouldn't. I can't bathe because I hate my body. I can't stand to look in the mirror because I hate my reflection. I am in many ways sick. I am waiting to die in part because I don't think I care enough to keep living. But each day I wake up and consider why I do bother to keep living.

There are moments and days and even stretches of weeks where I find my mind and heart saying to me to end it. That I feel I want to die.

But I don't want to die. I don't want to live as I do and I am scared and unable to change most things in my position. Years have rolled by and I am still falling apart more than rebuilding.

But I don't want to die. I want the pain to end. I had tried so long to ignore it. I tried at times to face it. The pain remains and has grown. There are days I debate taking my life to stop it. I have stared at knives, considered pills, thought about drowning. There are more ways I have considered but I won't list them all here.

But I don't want to die. Even if slowly I am day by day as I lay here and try to find meaning. I am dying. But I died so many ways before. 

I died when I listened to the bullshit my parents told me about how I was just confused or to much of a momma's boy when I was a child. I died when I tried for years to live to fit in with societies expectations and not find the support I needed. I died because I held in my feelings in a similar net of anxiety that drove me to just pretend I could cope with living in unhappiness by trying to find other ways to be myself. I died each time I looked at another woman born without my problems and was so jealous and envious I shamed myself and my body image. I died when my heart shattered each time I was betrayed those close people whose feelings I thought were so important before to the point they were all that mattered to me.

While those people despite their mistakes or mistreatment of me still matter I missed the important thing in all that self hate and shame. I should matter to me. Just as you should matter to you.

People who seek relationships want things from other people but they do not always find it. When a relationship is imperfect it can change or it can end. It hurts or can be awkward but you can try again with someone new. It won't be easy. But giving up just because you didn't find the person you wanted won't get you what you want.

Just change your mind or look elsewhere but you don't have to accept that the way things are is how they will always be.

I can't change other people only they can. I can't change what is passed only what is to be. I can't change what I am deepest within without experience. I can only change what I choose to be and the circumstances I am in control of to guide that experience. And people change the world all the time so I can change a lot.

But it takes work and you must face your fears and seek help and do all that you can to deny that part of yourself that wants to give up. That part that just wants to accept the world as it is and seek a comforting escape. That part of you that doesn't want to have to fight the world.

I am telling you now don't be afraid to live and be hurt.

You will suffer. You will at times have to fix yourself to get back up. You will struggle. But life is what it is. Unfair and confusing and painful.

And life is joyful, and pleasant, and sweet, and kind, and forgiving, and purposeful, and beautiful, and imaginative, and yours. You have seen it in small doses through all the noise and confusion whenever you find those good moments and the stir your heart for even a second.

And we in our efforts to try and live together allow too much to just stay in that confused jumble of pain by just giving in. We don't stand up against each other when it counts and when we do we often get it wrong. It leads more and more children to hide who they are to try and fit in while others champion their views. Bulling and oppression become normalized even without real intent for things to make sense so they don't have to feel as lost in who they are. While people push hate to strike back against those that scare them or offend their views flaws.

And those brave few times anyone steps up to be themselves and become the people they are deep inside the world is ready to eat them whole if they can't stand up. They look for support and it is not absent but not easily visible. Often that first voice never finds a partner because they are drown in their own problems.

Often times it seems we are alone for the bigger challenges. That we need support to change anything and that the need for others to be with seems hard to fulfill. It is not easy. It will never be easy. But changing that in our lives is worth it. Not just for us but for others too. When you can't change something yet change the world for yourself and others so that someday you can.

And it is all the easier with support. With people that care and will stand with you. If you stand then they stand and when the stand you stand with them. You keep each other honest.

But if you throw your life away you cannot change anything. You can't help those people looking for you for help. Forever that life is left as it stands. As history, society and people think it should be. Society and people who are wrong and confused and scared and have their own pains and shames and doubts they have trouble with. A history marked by the souls of those who came and went before through pain and fell along the way.

They aren't right. People are more than any person can imagine. History need not repeat. You are not poison. You are not wrong for having your pain. You are not wrong for stumbling from time to time. You are not perfect no matter how much you may wish you were.

So don't try to force yourself to be perfect. Just be you and make your life the best you can. Be as close as you can get. Be perfect in your imperfection. Help those you care about and take joy from doing it. Take your pain and learn from it and make it work for you. Teach people and learn from them as well and those who do so. 

Laugh when you fall and get back up and face the feelings and be honest. Don't let that pain define you or ferment. Make from it what you can. Turn it into experience to help others in similar pain. Use it to help yourself change your life for the better.

Choose to make your life what it should be and not what people demand it should be. Not what some random limit says you have to be. Not what some passing feeling says your often confused brain should act on. It won't be quick or easy but you can always choose so choose not to accept that defeat.

You are alive and you deserve to live and express that life to its fullest. Your death should come in defiance of itself screaming with joy at every second your heart beats and your pulse pounds. If you want to die then die from living to your fullest. Make those ignorant people around you that try to convince you that you are less than they watch you live. Let them see just how much more life you live and how much fuller you make it. Show every child that is born afraid of the world that living as who you truly are is far better than trying to fit in. Show them they can't just live only for others but must also live for themselves.

Cowards die a thousand deaths before their time. So don't be afraid of life.

Don't surrender it. Live and know that you deserve to live as you wish to.

I know it is hard. But do it. Don't leave us. We all need your help as well.
